extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office examiners and patent applicants/agents submitting/searching prior art and confidential materials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and documentation requirements for recording prior-art searches (Search Notes/Searched boxes), interference searches, and the submission, labeling, and Office handling of trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials in patent application/reexamination files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record field of search in first action
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits of an application, the examiner must record in the appropriate sections of the Official Correspondence 'Search Notes' form the areas in which the search for prior art was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also indicate the date(s) on which the search was conducted and provide the examiner's initials. See MPEP § 904.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record search updates in subsequent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In subsequent actions, where the search is brought up to date and/or where a further search is made, the examiner must indicate that the search has been updated and/or identify the additional field of search and include the date and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any search updates should include the appropriate databases and the search queries and classifications employed in the original search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate 'SEARCHED' boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Search Notes form includes three 'SEARCHED' boxes for recording searches in Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC), CPC Combination Sets and U.S. Patent Classification (USPC). When documenting a classification search, the examiner should ensure the proper box(es) is/are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record classification symbol, date, and initials
rubrics_metrics.description: When a classification search is performed, the classification symbol must be recorded in the appropriate 'SEARCHED' box section of the 'Search Notes' form along with the date that the search was performed (or updated) and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the classification search was limited, ensure how it was limited is made of record (see related guidance about printouts or annotations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make limitations of classification searches of record
rubrics_metrics.description: When the search is limited, the examiner must ensure that how the search was limited is made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most situations, the limitation will be apparent in a search history printout and the printout should be included with the 'Search Notes' form. If limited by an approach not apparent in the printout, annotate the 'SEARCH NOTES' box to explain the limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not merely list classification symbol if search was limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a search of all of the documents for a particular classification location was performed, it would be inaccurate to merely record the classification symbol in the 'SEARCHED' box without including the search history printout or indicating how the search was limited in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal importance of 'SEARCH NOTES' entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries made in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box are of equal importance to those placed in the 'SEARCHED' box. They are intended to complete the application file record of areas and/or documents considered by the examiner in their search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry must be dated and initialed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate how a classification search was limited in SEARCH NOTES
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotations indicating how a classification search was limited should be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box (each entry dated and initialed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-only database searches recorded in SEARCH NOTES
rubrics_metrics.description: If a text search was performed in a particular database and no classification search was performed, the following entry or its equivalent must be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box of the 'Search Notes' form: 'See search history printout(s)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the date(s) the search was performed (or updated) and the examiner’s initials, and include the search history printout in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record IPC searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches made within the International Patent Classification System (IPC) must be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record STIC and EIC searches and include printouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches performed by the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) or EIC must be recorded; the following entry or its equivalent must be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box: 'See search history printout(s)' along with the date that the search was performed (or updated) and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full text of any citations included in the search results will be provided at the examiner’s request. The complete search history printout must be included in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and supplement Internet search printouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the printout to determine if the Internet search engine name, the search logic, and the date of the search are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these are missing, write the missing information on the printout. Indicate all webpages reviewed. For Internet search engines, print out the first page and any pages that include names of webpages reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record consultations with other examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: A consultation with other examiners to determine if relevant search fields exist should be recorded in SEARCH NOTES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subclass is not searched, record the class and subclass, if any, discussed, followed by '(consulted).' This may include the name of the examiner consulted and the art unit (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document searches of electronic journals and books
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches performed in electronic journals and electronic books available through the STIC NPL website should be documented and examiners should contact EIC for assistance and to create a search history printout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document searches in other media/databases
rubrics_metrics.description: For searches performed in other media collections or databases (e.g., CD-ROM databases, specialized databases), record data as necessary to provide unique identification of material searched and sufficient information as to the search query or request so that the search can be updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the location of the database and its form (CD-ROM, etc.). Examples for citing CD-ROM databases are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document non-electronic (paper) literature searches
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonelectronic searches of publications in paper form (books, periodicals, abstracting publications), record specific identifying information (e.g., title, author, edition, volume, issue, pages, dates) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: Chem. Abs entries, Popular Mechanics, book citations, catalogs. Cursory browsing may be indicated collectively, but detailed reviews must be specifically recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record review of art cited in parent/related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of art cited in a parent application or an original patent (required for continuations, CIPs, divisionals, reissue, reexamination) must be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the application number of a parent application, followed by 'refs. checked' or 'refs. ck’ed.' Note exceptions if references not checked because not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record reviews of documents cited in PTAB trials
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of documents cited in a related trial before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board should be recorded (whether the claims have similar scope or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the trial number, document reviewed, U.S. Patent on trial and date reviewed; examples include IPR, PGR, CBM entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search history printout required for limited electronic searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time that a limited electronic search was performed (e.g., limited classified search or text search), a complete search history in the form of a printout must be included in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The search history must include minimum information: (A) all the search logic or chemical structure or sequence(s) used as a database query; (B) all the name(s) of the file(s) searched and the database service; (C) the date the search was made or updated; (D) an indication of the examiner who performed the search (e.g., user ID or initials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid including result printouts in search history
rubrics_metrics.description: A search history printout should be devoid of result printouts to limit the 'bulk search printouts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several search statements appear in the history, indicate which statement(s) produced the results that were reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence search documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding nucleotide and peptide sequence searches, these searches must be documented by printout(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of a printout for each database source searched must be included in the application file. Each printout must include all the information up to the 'ALIGNMENTS' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference search when application in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is in condition for allowance, an interference search must be made by using the most efficient and effective manner based on the claimed subject matter in the broadest claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: text search, classified search, or combination searches of US-PGPUB database in PE2E-SEARCH. Consider each effective filing date for CIPs. If claim directed to a nucleotide or peptide sequence, examiner must submit a request to STIC to perform an interference search of the sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record completion and limitations of interference search
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of the interference search should be recorded in the 'INTERFERENCE SEARCH' section of the 'Search Notes' form with an identification of the manner in which the interference search was limited (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A printout of only the database(s) searched, the query(ies) used (if any), and the date the interference search was performed must be made of record. The result printouts of the interference search must not be placed in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum search history elements (table summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search history printouts should include the history command/display that typically shows the search logic entered, the name of the database service, name of file(s) searched, and date of search when available from the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 lists database-specific history commands and indicates which elements are present for each database service; any missing elements may be documented by writing them on the printout or supplying further portions of the search transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling of trade secret/proprietary/protective order materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Information considered to be trade secret material, proprietary material, or subject to protective order must be clearly labeled as such and be filed in a sealed, clearly labeled, envelope or container.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each document or item must be clearly labeled as a 'Trade Secret' document or item, a 'Proprietary' document or item, or as an item or document 'Subject To Protective Order.' Avoid using terms 'Confidential,' 'Secret,' 'Restricted' or 'Restricted Data' (to avoid confusion with national security documents). If 'Subject to Protective Order,' the proceeding and tribunal must be set forth on each document or item. The envelope/container and each document must include complete identifying information for the file (Office/area, application details, TC Art Unit, Examiner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter and petition to expunge requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The envelope or container must be accompanied by a transmittal letter which contains the same identifying information and must state that the materials are considered trade secrets or proprietary or subject to a protective order and are being submitted for consideration under MPEP § 724.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.59 and fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)) to expunge the information, if found not to be material to patentability, should accompany the envelope or container.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended hand-delivery and mailing address
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure the envelope or container is not mishandled, the envelope or container should be hand-carried to the Customer Service Window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, the envelope or container may be mailed to the Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office receipt, artifact folder, and file notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, the transmittal letter and the envelope or container will be date stamped and brought to the attention of the examiner; the receipt will be noted on the 'Contents' of the application or reexamination file and the application will have a notation indicating trade secret/proprietary/protective order material has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will place the envelope or container in an Artifact folder. The words 'TRADE SECRET MATERIALS FILED WHICH ARE NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC' on the face of the file are sufficient to indicate the presence of trade secret material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of materials appropriate for MPEP § 724.02
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials contemplated for submission under MPEP § 724.02 include information 'material to patentability' but do not include information favorable to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, trade secret/proprietary/protective order materials required to be submitted under 37 CFR 1.56 or 1.555 can be submitted under MPEP § 724.02. Information favorable to patentability (e.g., evidence of commercial success) should not be submitted under § 724.02. Materials submitted in amendments/arguments/affidavits will be made of record and will not be given special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of submitted materials prior to determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP § 724.02 will be maintained in the original envelope or container (clearly marked 'Not Open To The Public') and will not be publicly available until a determination has been made as to whether or not the information is material to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to publication, an original application is not available to the public under 35 U.S.C. 122(a). After publication and if no petition to expunge was filed prior to mailing of notice of allowability or abandonment (or petition denied), materials will be released with other application papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if application abandoned before petition acted upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is to be abandoned, prior to the mailing of a notice of abandonment, the examiner will review the file and determine if a petition to expunge is in the file but not acted upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition to expunge has been filed, irrespective of materiality, the petition will be granted and the materials expunged. If no petition was filed, the materials will be available to the public under 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(ii) or (a)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if application allowed before petition acted upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is being allowed, prior to the mailing of a notice of allowability, the examiner (or other appropriate Office official) will make a determination as to whether any portion or all of the information submitted is material to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any portion or all is found material, the petition to expunge will be denied and the information will become part of the file history (and scanned if IFW). If all is found not material, the petition to expunge will be granted and the information expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for petition to expunge and public release
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition to expunge is not filed prior to the mailing of the notice of allowability, the materials submitted under MPEP § 724.02 will be released to the public upon issuance of the application as a patent and upon the filing of a request and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition to expunge under 37 CFR 1.59(b) will be treated according to MPEP § 724.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of materials submitted in reissue applications open to public
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP § 724.02 in a reissue application open to the public under 37 CFR 1.11(b) will be maintained separate from the reissue application file and will not be publicly available until a determination is made as to materiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They will only be released to the public with other application papers if no petition to expunge was filed prior to mailing of notice of allowability or abandonment, or if a petition was filed and denied.
